controls.control: R-A — a blocker that stood on the same cell last turn and is stationary now produces NO hold: the base's regressive detour on every turn
controls.why: the ruling of 20260825T094200Z: the standing is worthless exactly when the blocker will not move, and the never-moving worker is Candidate 2's tail, not this card's. This is the control that would catch R-A being silently absent

controls.control: R-A — rule-off is identical on the permanent-blocker situation
controls.why: with the revision in place the rule-on and rule-off arms now agree on this whole class, which is why the panel's 240-game parity is not the only evidence for it

controls.control: codex_1 #1 — a regressive block by a TRANSIENT blocker cycles H(b=1), H(b=2), R(b=0), H(b=1)
controls.why: the bound W is what stops a hold becoming a parked troll; if the counter did not reset on R the cycle would stall forever. SYNTHETIC: the probe declares the blocker to have arrived on each of the four turns, because under R-A a real blocker that stays put stops being transient after one turn. This control is about the COUNTER, not about how often the sequence occurs in play

controls.control: codex_1 #6a — the rule-off arm cannot emit H or a nonzero b on the same situation
controls.why: the parity claim rests on H being unreachable with the flag off

controls.control: codex_1 #2a — an IMPROVING detour after a prior hold is taken, as L, counter cleared
controls.why: the cure must not swallow the detours the base takes correctly

controls.control: codex_1 #2b — an EQUAL-distance detour after a prior hold is L0
controls.expected: NOT CONSTRUCTIBLE: on a 4-connected grid the BFS distances of adjacent cells differ by exactly one, and a free orthogonal neighbour of a reachable cell is itself reachable, so the manhattan fallback can never apply to one side of the comparison only. `toward_goal[detour] == d_cur` is unreachable and the predicate's `<=` is exactly `<`. The probe runs the sideways case against a TRANSIENT blocker and it resolves as H because the neighbour is d_cur+1, not equal.
controls.why: asked for by the G-0 ruling; reported honestly rather than faked

controls.control: codex_1 #3 — no legal detour after a prior hold is the base's forced WAIT, W, counter 0
controls.why: a hold must never be produced by the absence of a detour; that is the base's own branch

controls.control: codex_1 #4 — a free primary landing after a prior hold is P, counter cleared
controls.why: the counter counts CONSECUTIVE holds; a granted landing ends the run

controls.control: codex_1 #5 — a live own unit with no MOVE this turn is N, counter cleared
controls.why: definition 6: counters are reset for live own ids absent from command_by_id

controls.control: codex_1 #3b — a self-targeting MOVE resolved to WAIT is W0
controls.why: definition 3 names this case explicitly; it is the pre-pass, not the mover loop

controls.control: claude_1 — an earlier-order mover targeting a late-order holder's square resolves with ZERO own-troll contention

expected.one unseeded pass: u9 is granted u5's cell (1,0) while u5 holds on it
expected.the fixed point: u5 holds, u9 is NOT granted (1,0)

controls.why: this is the hazard that sent G-0 back REVISION_REQUIRED, and the two-phase fixed point is the ruling's repair for it; the single unseeded pass is printed beside it so the control shows the defect as well as the fix

controls.control: charter — the hold fires and the dance ends with PROGRESS
controls.expected: rule-on never emits R and ends no further from the target than rule-off; rule-off does step backwards on the same script
controls.why: a cure that merely stops the backward step and then stands still forever is the polite-standstill failure this programme has shipped before. REBUILT for revision R-A: the blocker is a teammate that has just ARRIVED on the cell and is busy this turn, then leaves — a permanent blocker no longer produces a hold at all and is covered by the R-A control above
